unlisted_practices: Establish clear, harmonized guidelines for the encoding, exchange, and provenance of annotations in digital pathology to enable interoperability, reproducibility, and scalable AI development.
Apply existing standards such as DICOM, ICC, and IHE PaLM rather than re-inventing them.
Adopt standards incrementally in value-aligned steps, prioritizing those with the highest regulatory, operational, or interoperability value.
Harmonize pre-analytical and analytical procedures, including staining protocols, tissue processing, and scanner configurations, to improve AI model generalizability.
Apply quality control standards to whole-slide images to detect artifacts such as blur, tissue folds, and air bubbles before AI training and use.
Use standardized formats such as OME-TIFF and DICOM to enable metadata embedding, version control, and reproducibility in AI workflows.
Use ICC color profiles to align color output across scanners and displays and reduce variability in computational image interpretation.
Develop standards for federated learning covering common data formats, aligned ontologies, and standardized performance metrics across institutions.
Develop standard frameworks for the generation, labeling, and validation of synthetic pathology images.
Develop standards for AI output formatting, provenance tracking, and model transparency to support explainability.
Develop standards for post-market surveillance, auditability, and explainability of continuously learning AI tools.
Manage standards through sustainable organizations, with both top-down oversight and bottom-up practicality.
Distinguish true standards from standard-adjacent tools by checking for formal consensus, explicit conformance requirements, and maintenance by a recognized standards body.

screen.reason: This is a concept paper/consensus framework from the Digital Pathology Association describing recommendations and standards for adopting and governing AI in digital pathology.
